rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters commit compound foolishness by assigning God partners without proof while disliking such an association for themselves.
rows.anchor: they were guilty of compound foolishness: in the first place, they imputed partners to God without having any grounds to do so

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabian idolaters ranked three deities highest, treating them as God's daughters who could persuade Him to grant their wishes.
rows.anchor: whom they thought to be beloved daughters of God and who could convince Him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrah al-Najm names Lāt, ʿUzzā, and Manāt, condemns the unjust preference for sons, and says these deities are invented names without revealed proof.
rows.anchor: They are but names which you and your fathers have invented in whose favour the Almighty has revealed no argument.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet asks no payment; he conveys his Lord's favors freely, so the people's refusal even to listen is astonishing.
rows.anchor: he is not asking them for any remuneration to listen to him and they are not being burdened by the amount

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge is cherished, and an upright person should hear unfamiliar guidance; refusing it resembles a blind person rejecting a hand that guides him.
rows.anchor: when someone tries to show him the way he shakes off his hand

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Arabs were ummī, they should have sought guidance, especially given the tradition since Ishmael that a prophet would bring light and guide the nations.
rows.anchor: The Arabs were ummī (not conversant with the sharī‘ah). As a result, they should have been seekers of God’s guidance

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rejecters had no access to the unseen, so should have embraced the Prophet's revealed guidance to God's directives.
rows.anchor: they had no such means. In this situation, it was only befitting that they lunge forward to grab the guidance he was providing them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They made a desire-based law for themselves but falsely treated it as religion revealed by God.
rows.anchor: totally based on their desires and fancies but they regarded it be the religion revealed to them by God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite lacking faith and good deeds, they claimed noble lineage guaranteed them Paradise, mocked the Prophet's warnings, and expected his death.
rows.anchor: people who were devoid of faith and virtuous deeds but claimed that since they were the progeny of nobles

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their excuses concealed fear that the Prophet's growing message would end their leadership; they spread fabrications to keep the masses from following him.
rows.anchor: they were foreseeing an end to their leadership with the expansion of the Prophet’s message.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse challenges their plotting and warns that the disbelievers themselves will be caught in their own scheme.
rows.anchor: those who disbelieve should remember that that they themselves will be caught in their own plot.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their fabricated arguments and allegations cannot save them when judgment arrives.
rows.anchor: will still not be able to save him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At his fate, the schemer will recognize that his own schemes and contrivances brought him to that end.
rows.anchor: When he encounters his fate, it will become evident to him that he reached this destination because of his own schemes and contrivances.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since everyone must ultimately face God, no other deity can rescue the idolaters from their plots' consequences; God is exalted above their partners.
rows.anchor: Do they think that they have some other gods besides God who will help them?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing contrary to God's established attributes can be ascribed to Him; the idolaters' religious innovations contradict attributes they themselves acknowledge.
rows.anchor: no attribute can be ascribed to God which is against His established and acknowledged attributes.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet cannot convince people bent on deception: even a visible punishment falling from heaven would be dismissed as layered clouds.
rows.anchor: they will regard it to be clouds stacked in layers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like Thamūd, who called the looming punishment a rain cloud, these rejecters will believe only when punishment strikes, when belief is too late.
rows.anchor: even then they did not believe it but reassured themselves by saying

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A preacher should answer doubts while they are sincere, but once someone uses reasoning to evade truth, further effort is useless and the matter should be left to God.
rows.anchor: Till that time, it is the obligation of a true preacher to try and dispel these doubts and objections.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rejecters are to be left until the Day of the trumpet's terror, depicted in Sūrah al-Ḥajj as people reeling like drunkards from God's punishment.
rows.anchor: The reference is to the Day which is portrayed thus in Sūrah al-Ḥajj:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that Day plots, supporters, companions, alleged deities, and intercessors will be useless; everyone faces God alone and is shown their deeds.
rows.anchor: their alleged deities and intercessors will be of no avail to them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the Hereafter, rejecters face worldly punishment as a divine practice; the Quraysh were humiliated and defeated during the Prophet's lifetime.
rows.anchor: as per a divine practice was necessarily faced by the people who denied their respective messengers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in the expression for patience indicates that ṣabr also carries the sense of waiting for the Lord's decision with perseverance.
rows.anchor: the word patience also encompasses the meaning of waiting.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assurance that the Prophet is before God's eyes expresses affection and constant protection, so conspiracies cannot harm him.
rows.anchor: the Prophet (sws) is always in the eyes of God which implies that he is always under His protection.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet gains patience through diligent prayer, particularly tahajjud; the phrase about rising is explained by 26:217–218.
rows.anchor: he should be as diligent as he can in prayer, in particular the tahajjud prayer.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night-glorification wording recurs with slight variation in Sūrah Qāf, where its exegesis is given; the qualification of tasbīḥ by ḥamd is explained elsewhere.
rows.anchor: also occur thus in Sūrah Qāf

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrah al-Najm is the counterpart of al-Ṭūr: both substantiate reward and punishment, though al-Ṭūr highlights torment and al-Najm refutes false intercession.
rows.anchor: The central theme of both sūrahs is the same: substantiation of reward and punishment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: False belief in intercession makes threats ineffective, so the Qur'an repeatedly joins monotheism and the Hereafter to close this escape route.
rows.anchor: For this very reason, the Qur’ ān has always mentioned tawḥīd and the Hereafter side by side

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters rely on deities that are merely invented names, not real intercessors.
rows.anchor: they are mere names which they have invented

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if intercessors existed, they could not add to God's knowledge, change His judgment, or turn falsehood into truth; He judges with perfect justice.
rows.anchor: there is no possibility that on that day the intercession of someone may add to His information or change His decision or turn falsehood into truth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing verse of al-Ṭūr, mentioning the stars' decline, dovetails with al-Najm's opening oath by the star as it descends.
rows.anchor: very aptly dovetails into the opening verse of this sūrah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic coherence can link wording, implied meanings, or both, as in the transition between these sūrahs.
rows.anchor: at some places, this link is between the words, at others between the meanings implied

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 1–18 establish that the recited Qur'an is not soothsaying or fortune-telling but was revealed to the Prophet by God's trusted, dependable angel.
rows.anchor: not the work of a soothsayer or a fortune-teller

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse presents every verse as true and inevitable, and rejects the idea that the Prophet's experiences of revelation and Gabriel are illusions.
rows.anchor: All its verses are based on the truth and what is stated in them is inevitable
